question.leadin: In his pseudo-historical book 1421, Gavin Menzies claimed that an explorer from this dynasty visited the Americas before Christopher Columbus.
question.text: Name this Chinese dynasty, renowned for its blue and white porcelain, which succeeded the Yuan dynasty and preceded the Qing dynasty.
question.clue: Under this dynasty's Yongle emperor, seven voyages by the mariner Zheng He explored the Indian Ocean.

swap.leadin: During this rebellion, a Muslim group called the Hansu Braves set fire to Hanlin Academy during the Siege of the Foreign Legations.
swap.text: Name this rebellion which occurred during the Qing [Ching] dynasty and was defeated by the Eight-Nation Alliance.
swap.answerHtml: Boxer Rebellion [or Boxer Uprising; or other synonyms for “rebellion;” or Yihetuan Movement]
swap.clue: Edward Seymour's forces were stymied by cut rail lines before they could reach the capital.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Chinese history.
question.text: This rebellion's leader, Hong Xiuquan, claimed to be the brother of Jesus, and it attempted to establish a "Heavenly Kingdom" in mid-nineteenth century China.
question.clue: This conflict's Battle of Cixi saw the death of Frederick Ward, and Zeng Guofan's Xiang Army took its capital of Nanjing.

swap.leadin: This event occurred in the wake of the death of the reformer Hu Yaobang.
swap.text: Name this set of student protests crushed by Deng Xiaoping in the June Fourth Massacre. During these protests, students constructed the "Goddess of Democracy."
swap.clue: This event sparked by the death of Hu Yaobang was crushed by 300,000 soldiers sent by Deng Xiaoping ("shiao-PING").

question.text: This Jin capital city was also called Zhongdu, and served as the capital of the Qing and Yuan dynasties following the Mongol conquest.
question.clue: 12 bronze animal sculptures were among the few artifacts that survived the destruction of the Old Summer Palace in this city as ordered by Lord Elgin in the Second Opium War.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the various conquests of the Khans not named Genghis.
swap.text: This Khan established the Yuan Dynasty after conquering the Song Dynasty of China.
swap.clue: This man began construction of a new capital at Dadu and he was ultimately succeeded by his grandson, Temur.

question.text: This name is given to the era preceding the Warring States period, during which royal authority began to decline. It takes its poetic name from a set of Annals traditionally attributed to Confucius.
question.clue: That royal family's flight from Zongzhou to Chengzhou initiated this time period, which the rise of the states of Wu and Yue.

swap.text: After being overthrown by the National Liberation Council, this politician granted Nkrumah refuge in his country. This first Premier of the People's Republic of China created the "Four Modernizations" economic policy.
swap.clue: In 1971 his strategy of improving ties with the U.S. was cemented when he met Henry Kissinger in Peking.

question.text: The French team was astonished to find the Chinese head coach studying this text for basketball strategy during timeouts. Billions of people learned sayings like "a revolution is not a dinner party" from this text.
question.answerHtml: The Little Red Book [or Quotations from Chairman Mao Tse-tung; or Máo Zhǔxí Yǔlù]
question.clue: In many "big character posters," workers and soldiers are shown smiling and holding this text high in the air.

swap.text: The anecdote about the Bai Qi (bye chee), "The Human Butcher," appears in this text by Sima Qian (suh-mah chee-EN), which claims that the Xia (sh'YAH) Dynasty were the first rulers in the lands that comprise modern-day China.
swap.clue: This text describes the melting of thousands of enemy weapons to create twelve colossal metal statues, a loyalty test in which a man points to a deer and calls it a horse, and the "rectification of weights and measures."

question.text: After the Ten Attendants were removed from power, this period of Chinese history occurred and was named for the land divided between Wei, Wu, and Shu. The Jin Dynasty succeeded this period.
question.clue: In the lead up to this period, one side lost the Battle of Red Cliffs.

swap.text: The Silla Kingdom allied with this Chinese dynasty to conquer its neighbors. This dynasty was interrupted by Wu Zetian's short-lived Zhou Dynasty.
swap.clue: This dynasty lost the battle of Talas to the Abbasids.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the career of the Chinese polymath Zhang Heng.
question.text: Zhang invented an early one of these devices, which consisted of a jar with eight dragon heads surrounded by frogs. Historians theorize a pendulum would knock a ball out into a frog mouth when the device was activated.
question.answerHtml: seismometer [or seismograph; prompt on descriptions like earthquake detectors and such]

swap.leadin: The death of one of these people named Feng Guozhang ("fung gwuh-jong") and the rise of the Constitutional Protection movement led to the first of a sequence of open conflicts between these people.
swap.text: What people dominated a namesake era of post-Qing China and headed cliques based in Zhili ("jirr-lee"), Anhui ("ahn-hwei") and Fengtian ("fung-tyen")?
swap.clue: Many of these figures gave up power after they lost the Central Plains War.

question.leadin: For their role in this mission, Colonel David Barrett never received promotion and John Service was arrested and driven out of the State Department.
question.text: Name this World War II diplomatic and intelligence-gathering mission to Yenan. It takes its name from the fact that the Americans were traveling into "rebel" territory to meet with Chinese Communists.
question.answerHtml: Dixie Mission [or United States Army Observation Group in Yenan]
question.clue: This mission which arrived in Yan'an ("yen-AHN") in 1944. John S. Service, a member of this mission, was purged from the State Department after being accused of treason in Joseph McCarthy's Wheeling speech.

swap.text: Amidst widespread instability and collapse of the monetary system, the Yuan ("ywen") dynasty was overthrown by these rebellions, an offshoot of the White Lotus movement.
swap.answerHtml: Red Turban rebellions [or Hóngjīn Qǐyì; accept answers with synonyms for “rebellion”]

question.text: This city was capital of the Song dynasty until its capture by the Jin during the Jingkang Incident. A substantial Jewish population in this city survived until modern times.
question.clue: The scroll painting Along the River During the Qingming Festival likely depicts the splendor of this capital city before its final two emperors, Qinzong ("cheen-dzong") and Huizong ("hway-dzong"), were captured in the Jingkang Incident.

swap.leadin: Many courtesans were trained at a performing arts academy in this city nicknamed "the Pear Garden."
swap.text: Name this city, where an imperial consort held a comic ceremony whereby she wrapped a general in a large silk diaper. This city also contains the Great Wild Goose Pagoda.
swap.answerHtml: Xi’an (“shee-AHN”) [or Chang’an] (Yang Guifei wrapped An Lushan in a diaper.)
swap.clue: The Silk Road had its eastern origin in this city, where Emperor Qin Shi Huangdi was buried with his Terracotta Army.

question.text: This Chinese monk recounted Harsha's defeat at the Narmada River as part of the Great Tang Records on the Western Regions that he wrote in his 17 years of travelling through India, which were inspired by Faxian.
question.clue: The Monkey King must defend this monk from demons who want to gain immortality by eating him. While conducting the ceremony of Shui Lu Da Hui, this man is told to make a pilgrimage to the Western Heaven.

swap.text: Tsai was a chief drafter of the special state-to-state relations doctrine pursued by this predecessor of Chen. Nicknamed "Mr. Democracy," this first directly elected President of Taiwan partially initiated the Third Taiwan Straits Crisis by making a 1995 visit to his alma mater, Cornell.
swap.clue: In the 1980s, this person nicknamed "Mr. Democracy" asserted that his country's claims to the Spratly Islands were exactly the same as China's. This person's trip to his alma mater Cornell in 1995 precipitated a military standoff between China and the US.
